articles.body:
We're back with another action-packed weekend of European soccer!

In the Premier League, Aston Villa kept up their recent success at home over Manchester City to win 2-1 and end City's 100% start to the season. Defending champions Arsenal host Everton at the Emirates Stadium looking to go level at the top of the table, while Coventry City take on Fulham at the same time.

Later, we wrap up the Premier League slate with a London derby, as Xabi Alonso's Chelsea face Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge.

Elsewhere, Arsenal's women beat rivals Spurs 2-1 in the WSL, Napoli host AS Roma in a huge Serie A showdown, while Borussia Dortmund welcome Eintracht Frankfurt to Signal Iduna Park.

Enjoy all the action from Saturday's matches across Europe.

articles.headline: Ex-NBA player Malik Beasley negotiating plea deal in gambling case
articles.description: Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with Department of Justice lawyers over his alleged role in a bribery and betting scheme, one of his attorneys confirmed.
articles.headlineJa: 元NBAのマリク・ビーズリー、賭博事件で司法取引を交渉中
articles.descriptionJa: 元NBA選手のマリク・ビーズリーが、贈収賄および賭博スキームへの関与の疑いを巡り、司法省の検察官と司法取引の交渉を行っていることが、弁護士の一人によって確認された。
articles.body:
Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with Department of Justice lawyers over his alleged role in a bribery and betting scheme, one of his attorneys confirmed Saturday.

An overnight notice on the court docket indicated that Beasley, who played for six NBA teams over a nine-year career, intends to plead guilty in the case. Attorney Steve Haney told ESPN in a text message that Beasley has not signed a plea deal with prosecutors but that talks are ongoing and a decision is expected early this week.

A spokesperson for the Eastern District of New York did not immediately reply to follow-up questions about the matter.

Prosecutors allege that Beasley, 29, deliberately manipulated his statistics in at least four games during the 2023-24 season while he was with the Milwaukee Bucks so that gamblers could place and win bets on his performances.

According to the indictment, his co-defendants selected games that would not be nationally televised and Beasley decided whether he would underperform or overperform his scoring and rebounding.

Though he had earned tens of millions of dollars during his career, Beasley also accumulated "multimillion-dollar gambling losses" when he became part of the alleged scheme, according to the indictment.

Beasley faces federal counts of bribery in sporting contests, wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy. He initially pleaded not guilty to all of the charges.

Late Friday, however, the judge overseeing his case asked a federal magistrate in Brooklyn to schedule a hearing for Beasley to change his plea. The judge filed a similar order Friday for another defendant in the case, Ernesto Plascencia. Plascencia's attorney confirmed Saturday morning that he will be entering a guilty plea.

One of the other defendants in the case, William Brown, pleaded guilty earlier this month, while fellow sports bettor Robert Gorodetsky is slated to formally enter a guilty plea Nov. 20.

Former NBA player Ed Davis and Paolo Zamorano, who was Davis' agent, were also charged in the case and have pleaded not guilty.

ABC News contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' but could be away for weeks after collapsing
articles.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: バイエルンのヴィンセント・コンパニーは「容態安定」、失神により数週間の離脱の可能性
articles.descriptionJa: バイエルン・ミュンヘンのヴィンセント・コンパニー監督が、前日のトレーニング中に失神した原因を特定するため、さらなる検査を受けることになったとクラブが土曜日に発表した。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

articles.headline: Man City beaten by double from Aston Villa's Jackson
articles.description: Nicolas Jackson scored twice to lead Aston Villa to a 2-1 win over Manchester City.
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Manchester City's perfect start to the Premier League season ended Saturday with a 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

Nicolas Jackson scored both goals for Villa against Enzo Maresca's City, who were aiming for an eighth straight win in the league.

It also extended Villa's outstanding recent run to six wins from seven games in all competitions.

Jackson is up to seven goals for the season in all competitions. He fired the opener inside six minutes at Villa Park.

Erling Haaland headed City level in the second half, but Jackson got his second and the winner with a first-time finish that squirmed under goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

City fell to a fourth defeat at Villa Park in as many seasons.

articles.headline: Man City lose 100% Premier League record with defeat at Aston Villa
articles.description: Manchester City suffered defeat for the first time in the Premier League this season after Nicolas Jackson's double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park.
articles.body:
Manchester City suffered defeat for the first time in the Premier League this season when Nicolas Jackson's double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park.

Unai Emery's side continued its turnaround in form after a slow start to the campaign and picked up a fourth straight win across all competitions, and its first league victory at home this season.

Manchester City do not enjoy visiting Villa Park and have now lost their last four league games there, while Enzo Maresca saw his 100% league start as City boss vanish.

Another tough afternoon in the West Midlands started when Marc Guéhi's mistake allowed Jackson to give Villa an early lead.

Villa had keeper Zion Suzuki to thank for making several vital saves, and Iliman Ndiaye crashed an effort off the post as Villa held strong to take the lead into the break.

Erling Haaland grabbed his ninth league goal of the season to get City level, but Jackson buried his second of the afternoon -- his fourth of the season -- on the hour mark to hand Villa the points.

The visitors were greeted with more boos from an away ground ahead of kickoff after they were found guilty of serious breaches of the competition's financial regulations last month.

City conceded a corner after Gianluigi Donnarumma took too long to take his goal kick, which put City on the back foot, and Villa's quick start was rewarded with the opener in the sixth minute.

Guéhi was unable to control the ball and instead spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it into Jackson, and he expertly finished into the top of the net.

The early goal did not dent City's confidence, and they were denied an equalizer when Suzuki sprang right to push Ndiaye's curling effort away.

The Japan goalkeeper was getting busier by the minute. He put out an outstretched arm to thwart Rayan Cherki following some neat footwork by Jérémy Doku before stopping Abdukodir Khusanov from range.

Ndiaye had already threatened Suzuki once by cutting inside and letting one rip, and he did it again, only to see the effort slam off the outside of the post.

Haaland had a quiet first half but made his contribution seven minutes after the break to get City level when he nodded Ndiaye's cross past Suzuki.

City's onslaught continued and Villa's woodwork was rattled again; this time Suzuki tipped Josko Gvardiol's ferocious strike off the bar.

And that save proved decisive as Villa retook the lead just as it looked like City were turning up the heat on the hour mark.

Villa turned defense into attack with precision. Victor Lindelöf's ball set them on the front foot and it ended up with substitute Ibrahim Mbaye, and his first major contribution was to tee up Jackson, who saw his strike squeeze past Donnarumma.

articles.headline: Curtis Jones: Serie A too slow? Inter arrival explains Liverpool similarity
articles.description: Inter Milan midfielder Curtis Jones insists Serie A is no different to the Premier League when it comes to playing for the top clubs.
articles.body:
Inter Milan midfielder Curtis Jones insists Serie A is no different to the Premier League when it comes to playing for the top clubs.

The 25-year-old joined the league champions from Liverpool in the summer and has adapted well to Italian football.

But he rejected suggestions Serie A is easier than its English counterpart.

"From the outside, everyone thinks that Serie A is a slower league and that the level is not that high. I only partially agree," Jones told DAZN.

"The games are slower because of the way opponents face us. At Liverpool, it was exactly the same.

"Being one of the strongest teams in the league, opponents rarely came to press us, but they made everything more difficult with a low block.

"If you are the strongest team, with the best players, this is what the opponents will do. In Italy as in England."

Jones has quickly become a fan favourite, with a video recently circulating on social media of a coachload of supporters wearing masks depicting his face and singing his name.

The Scouser said he felt there was a similarity between Milan and his home city in that respect.

"When we played against Inter in the Champions League, I immediately noticed the connection between players and fans," he added.

"I and Liverpool have always had this kind of special bond with the fans, our 12th man on the pitch.

- Liverpool's Andoni Iraola urges Rio Ngumoha not to be distracted by 'outside noise'

- The story behind Ronald Araujo, Liverpool's new fan favorite

- Ronald Araújo: 'Finding what I needed' at Liverpool

"I think for those who love Inter the same thing applies so it was an easy choice [to join]."

The league leaders suffered another injury blow ahead of the visit of struggling Fiorentina.

Scans on Friday revealed wing-back Luis Henrique, who was a late substitute in the midweek Champions League win over Shakhtar Donetsk, had sustained an adductor strain.

The Brazilian is likely to be out until after next month's international break.

articles.headline: Amen Thompson stuffs Wembanyama's last-second shot as Rockets hold off Spurs
articles.description: Amen Thompson blocked Victor Wembanyama at the rim to prevent a potential tying bucket as the Rockets beat the Spurs 114-110.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas -- Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson couldn't quite explain what happened after sealing a 114-110 victory over the San Antonio Spurs by swatting away a last-gasp attempt at the rim by Victor Wembanyama.

In the aftermath of the game-saving play, Rockets forward Kevin Durant scurried over in excitement to deliver Thompson a message Friday as the sellout crowd at Moody Center groaned in disbelief.

"I said, 'What the f--- is wrong with him, thinking he was just going to lay it up so easily?'" Durant recalled.

"I don't know," Thompson shot back.

With five seconds remaining and Houston clinging to a 112-110 lead, Spurs point guard De'Aaron Fox floated a pass over Rockets forward Jabari Smith Jr. to Wembanyama, just as the big man spun toward the basket outside the restricted area. Wembanyama soared for what usually ends with a dunk. But Wembanyama's 8-foot wingspan couldn't clear Thompson's 7-foot reach and pogo-stick leaping ability.

"I just knew they were going to try to get probably me or one of the other smaller guys on him," Thompson said. "I jump pretty high, so I wouldn't try to keep ducking [in on] me."

Thompson smacked Wembanyama's attempt into the waiting hands of Fred VanVleet, who iced the game with a pair of free throws.

"Man, what an incredible block," Durant said. "It was just insane, man. As soon as your feet hit the ground, to be able to bounce back up so quick, that's rare in any human. To be 6-7, dunk the ball and block shots like a center is insane."

Thompson finished with a team-worst minus-12 on the box score. But what transpired on the floor told a different story for the 23-year-old, who finished with 20 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and a pair of steals.

"We did a really good job of switching and denying some catches, pushed [Wembanyama] off his spot, did his work early instead of getting ducked in like we did quite a few times," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said. "And from there, he uses athleticism and God-given ability there and did a hell of a job one-on-one with him in the post."

Thompson worked Wembanyama on the offensive end too. With 1:13 left in the third quarter, Thompson cut to the basket for a two-hand jam over the Frenchman off an assist by Durant. Wembanyama fouled Thompson on the play, and the Rockets guard nailed the and-1 free throw to give Houston a nine-point lead.

"That's low-key getting dunked on, right?" Thompson said, smiling.

Thompson and Durant scored 20 points apiece, but Rockets center Alperen Sengun dominated Wembanyama and the rest of the Spurs bigs to pour in a game-high 29 points with seven rebounds and seven assists. The performance marked his 35th career game with 25 points, five rebounds and five assists, tying Steve Francis for the second-most such games by a Rockets player before age 25.

Sengun scored 18 points in the second half, including 14 in the fourth quarter, to help Houston get off to its first 2-0 start since 2017-18.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick provides Man United injury updates, demands mental preparation
articles.description: Under-fire Michael Carrick says his players must be mentally prepared to move on if misfiring Manchester United are to end their winless run against Bournemouth.
articles.body:
Under-fire Michael Carrick says his players must be mentally prepared to move on if misfiring Manchester United are to end their winless run against Bournemouth.

Old Trafford once again finds itself in the eye of a storm after Wednesday's 4-1 capitulation at Champions League new boys Como raised serious questions over the manager's future.

Captain Bruno Fernandes compounded matters when appearing to question United's approach in Italy, where Carrick expressed anger with his players and went over to the supporters to apologise at full-time.

The Red Devils, now without a win in seven games, were without nine players in Como and again have absentees to deal with as the manager looks to ease mounting pressure at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

"Ayden [Heaven] is back with group," Carrick said. "He was suffering from illness but is back around the group and then we'll see what the next couple of days bring [for the others].

"It's more mentally now. Physically, the boys are recovering from a game and there is only so much training you can do out on the grass.

"It's more mental and being prepared for what's next."

Leny Yoro is available to face Bournemouth having missed the trip to Italy through suspension, with outspoken Lisandro Martínez facing a race to be fit to face Bournemouth.

Marcus Rashford has been dealing with a hip complaint, while Benjamin Sesko, Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw remain sidelined along with Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte.

Such injury issues are blow for a United side that have failed to beat Bournemouth in their last six meetings, with Erik ten Hag overseeing their last win in this fixture 41 months ago.

- Man United's worst league starts ever: How does 2026-27 compare?

- Carrick refuses to rule out dropping Bruno Fernandes for Man United clash with Bournemouth

- Michael Carrick: Under-pressure Man United boss '100%' backs himself amid tension

Casemiro scored the one goal and played an important role in Carrick's fine start to a job that he is fighting to hold onto as he made an impassioned call for humility and self-sacrifice on Friday.

"I think it's pretty clear as day," the United boss said. "I'm not telling you anything new.

"I haven't definitely invented anything new. That's the make-up of any good football team. You have to earn the right to be better than your opponent.

"You have to do more than your opponent to win a game. That's as simple as that. It doesn't change. It never changes. That's what we need to do to win more games."

articles.headline: NFL House in Paris closes ahead of street protests in French capital
articles.description: The NFL closed its "NFL House" in Paris as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up.
articles.body:
PARIS -- The NFL closed its "NFL House" in Paris on Saturday as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up.

The league announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning through its "OnePass" app and it came a day after closing its pop-up NFL shop - in both cases citing "potential accessibility issues."

Security concerns have overshadowed the NFL's debut in Paris. The New Orleans Saints will play the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in the league's first-ever regular-season game in France.

Also Saturday, the Saints announced that " Saints House has been postponed until Sunday."

Events planned Saturday at NFL House included "French Athletes in Football" and "From the Field to the Community."

Major museums including the Louvre and Orsay Museum are closed Saturday, though tourists were lined up to enter Notre Dame Cathedral. French authorities are intent on preventing a repeat of recent violent unrest.

The U.S. State Department this week issued a security alert that cautioned "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" to "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings" because of protests.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said this week that preparations were made in consultation with U.S. and French authorities. Street protests, he said, "are not unusual in France."

On Friday, French President Emmanuel Macron met with Goodell along with Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers owners Art Rooney II at the Élysée Palace to "discuss Sunday's game and the long-term future of the NFL in Paris."

The NFL said Friday that its pop-up shop in the city center would be closed Saturday but that fans could use an alternative shop set up at Stade de France, located north of the city in Saint-Denis.

A weekend event for Steelers fans was canceled Thursday because of security concerns.

articles.headline: Will Niners have edge with ex-Falcons coach facing Penix?
articles.description: With all of the familiarity between Morris and the Falcons, Sunday's game should come down to execution.
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Bijan Robinson has maintained a close relationship with Raheem Morris. It makes sense. Morris was the Atlanta Falcons' head coach for two of the first three seasons of Robinson's career.

On Sunday, the two men will meet again under different circumstances.

Robinson will be helping to lead the Falcons' offense as one of the top running backs in the league. Morris, who has called Robinson the best player in the NFL multiple times, will be back in Atlanta as the San Francisco 49ers' defensive coordinator. Morris was fired as Atlanta's coach in January after back-to-back eight-win campaigns.

Robinson said he spoke to Morris just a few weeks ago, and he's relishing the chance to face off against a man he calls a "father figure" to him.

"He's always going to be family to me no matter if we compete or not," Robinson said. "But yeah, man, he still talks to all of his players, because that's just who he is."

Morris is glad Penix has recovered from the torn left ACL that ended his season last year on Nov. 16.

"He's back healthy and he's probably everything that you thought and hoped for as far as being a play-action passer, a guy that can push the ball down the field, can make all the throws, go through the whole process," Morris said. "Just one of those guys that I have a lot of appreciation for and love for."

The Falcons players on offense who have been here the past several years will be going up against a defense run by a man who knows them all too well.  And that 49ers defense has been potent regardless of opponent familiarity. San Francisco is allowing the fourth-fewest points per game (18.3) and the fifth-fewest yards per game (300).

Atlanta (2-4) must perform against Morris and the undefeated Niners or risk losing three straight games and moving to 0-4 at home. A fifth loss in the first seven games is not how the Falcons wanted to start off under new head coach Kevin Stefanski.

The Falcons' biggest issue on offense is one the Chicago Bears exploited last week in a 31-23 Falcons loss. The Bears pressured quarterback Michael Penix Jr. 46.2% of the time, the highest rate Penix has faced this season. Chicago sacked Penix five times and blitzed on more than half of his dropbacks.

The results were not good. For the season, Penix has the worst EPA per dropback under quick pressure in the NFL (-1.17). He is 3-of-15 for 17 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions in those scenarios.

With no pressure at all, Penix has the fourth-best EPA per dropback in the league (0.40). So, it is imperative that the Falcons figure out how to better protect him.

"Any game you go into, you want to protect your quarterback," Stefanski said. "And I think you protect your quarterback literally with the protection, but also you protect the quarterback with how guys get open, how we get the ball out of our hands, how we run the ball, all those type of things."

No defensive coordinator knows Penix better than Morris. He was part of the regime

articles.headline: Fernando Mendoza is embracing being Raiders' latest Hispanic QB
articles.description: The rookie's next chapter is inspired by the legacies of a Hispanic coach, QB and a Raiders' fan base embracing the culture.
articles.body:
IN HIGH SCHOOL in 2021, Fernando Mendoza watched former Texas A&M quarterback Zach Calzada, a Cuban American like himself, and wondered about other Cubans and Hispanic quarterbacks who played at the next level. More importantly, he wanted to know how many of them had success in the NFL, even winning Super Bowls --- a dream of his.

A Google search opened Mendoza's eyes. He researched Tom Flores and Jim Plunkett, who are considered trailblazers for Latinos in the sport. Flores (Mexican American) was the first Hispanic quarterback in the NFL in 1960 when he debuted for the Oakland Raiders -- who are now based in Las Vegas. Plunkett, also Mexican American, was a college standout at Stanford, winning the Heisman Trophy in 1970 before being drafted by the New England Patriots with the first overall pick in 1971.

Plunkett is the first Hispanic American player to win the Heisman Trophy and be drafted No. 1.

Flores and Plunkett simultaneously became the first Hispanic coach and first Hispanic quarterback to win a Super Bowl. The duo helped the Raiders defeat the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl XV in 1981 -- the first of two Super Bowls that they won together. Plunkett was named the game's Most Valuable Player.

"To see that example [and] to know whatever I am doing, it is possible, meant a great deal to me," Mendoza told ESPN.

As the Raiders' No. 1 pick in April's draft, Mendoza is now doing more than just viewing Flores and Plunkett as inspirational figures. Mendoza is continuing their legacy. Should Mendoza start for the Raiders, he'll join another No. 1 pick in Carolina Panthers QB Bryce Young as the only starting quarterbacks of Hispanic descent in the NFL this season.

Regardless of whether he wants to be, he is a beacon of hope for the Raiders, with a fairly large Hispanic fan base. Flores and Plunkett symbolize the franchise's glory days, and they believe Mendoza can help bring the team back to relevance. Mendoza understands the role bestowed upon him can be pressure and a privilege. At the same time, it's added motivation for him to have a career that can be an inspiration for others who look like him.

"It's a great sense of pride knowing that it's been done before and it can be done; winning a championship [while] being Hispanic as the focal point," Mendoza said. "However, it's also a great deal of pressure, and that's something I take upon myself whenever I make decisions."

WHEN MENDOZA ARRIVED in Las Vegas after April's 2026 NFL draft, the magnitude of his presence was evident. The Raiders have not been to the postseason since 2021, which was the last year they finished with a winning record. The organization hasn't been to the Super Bowl since 2002 and hasn't hoisted the Vince Lombardi Trophy since Plunkett and Flores led the Raiders to a victory over the Washington Commanders in Super Bowl XVIII in 1984.

articles.headline: Inside the silent messages Boye Mafe sends every game day
articles.description: The Bengals defensive end uses sign language to say "I love you" to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- Before the chaos of each game unfolds, Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Boye Mafe has a conversation that centers him in a special place.

He closes his eyes and starts talking to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018. And in those moments, Mafe lays out his vision for what's about to unfold.

I know you're watching over me. I want to put on a show for you. I love you and this is what I'm going to do for you.

Then he'll wrap up the message by using American Sign Language to say "I love you" before he continues the rest of his pregame routine. Mafe does the same after each sack.

But it's about more than signs. Everything Mafe does is about what he signals. From those messages to Bola, to his pregame outfits, to how he plays, it's all about honoring the systems and structures that built him into one of the NFL's leading pass rushers and a Super Bowl champion.

"I try not to let circumstances dictate who I am," Mafe told ESPN. "At the end of the day, I am who I am and I want to be true to who I am."

That doesn't come easily. Mafe, the son of proud Nigerians, grapples with a phenomenon that is common among those with generational ties to other places -- the more time passes, the harder it is to stay connected to those roots.

But all it takes is one glance on game day to see just how strong those ties are.

How Boye Mafe's mother impacted her community

To fully understand why Mafe signs to his late mother requires understanding his upbringing in the western suburbs of Minneapolis.

Mafe and his siblings often communicate via American Sign Language. Starting with his older sister, Tayo, they all decided to study it in high school as their alternative language. And over the years the practice has stuck, even during games. Once, Tayo recalled signing to Mafe when he suffered an injury at Minnesota. He quickly signaled back that it wasn't anything serious.

Of all Mafe's six siblings, he is the one who spent the most time in their mother's seamstress shop on 1110 Lowery Avenue in North Minneapolis. There, Bola did more than mend clothes. She served as a cultural hub for many, not just Nigerians or those with Yoruba roots.

And she invested in the community. She volunteered at a battered women's shelter, made vests for Mafe's entire church choir and often let her customers have some extended credit.

"She had a lot of patience because sometimes people couldn't pay and she was like, 'Oh, pay me later,'" said Angie Onayiga, one of Bola's longtime friends. "She still gave them the clothes, sold things for them."

When Bola was diagnosed with cancer while Boye was in high school, the bond between mother and son deepened. Boye and his brother Domi did everything they could to make sure Bola was as comfortable as possible as the disease progressed.

How she fought the disease made a lasting impact on Boye.

articles.headline: NFL Week 7 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
articles.description: Touchdowns for Tucker Kraft and Germie Bernard? Cardinals pull another upset? Revenge game for Trey Hendrickson? Let's predict 15 things for Week 7.
articles.body:
Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Bears beat the Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Can the Cardinals pull off an upset for the second straight week? What could Packers tight end Tucker Kraft's stat line look like against the Lions? Is Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee a sneaky play in fantasy? And how many sacks will Ravens edge rusher Trey Hendrickson have against his former team?

Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Arizona Cardinals +4.5 (+195 moneyline) vs. Denver Broncos

The Broncos haven't shown they can pull away when ahead this season. Denver is averaging only 3.4 yards per carry (third lowest in the league), and quarterback Bo Nix has thrown for just 230 yards over the past two games combined. Despite a strong showing against the Rams, Arizona's pass defense has given up plenty of explosive plays in 2026. But Denver rarely throws downfield to take advantage.

The Broncos' defense should be a tough matchup for Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett, so I'm not expecting a big offensive day from the Cardinals. But this matchup looks like it will be decided by a field goal, and Arizona could come out on top.

Kansas City Chiefs +2.5 (+120 moneyline) at Seattle Seahawks

Kansas City has the defense to keep this close even if Seattle slows down QB Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs create pressure on nearly 39% of dropbacks, and QB Sam Darnold has completed only 38% of his throws under pressure this season. Seattle's struggles with run blocking could leave him handling too many difficult passing downs.

Offensively, running back Kenneth Walker III faces a tough rushing matchup against his former team, but Seattle has had issues covering RBs as receivers. That gives Kansas City another way to move the ball and win this outright.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Tucker Kraft, TE, Green Bay Packers: 9 targets, 7 receptions, 87 receiving yards, 1 TD

Kraft has the benefit of going against a Lions defense that has allowed 27% of its targets to opposing tight ends, the second-highest rate in the league. But it gets better. Based on player tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats, Detroit linebackers Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes and Jack Campbell all bite on play-action more than average. The Packers haven't used play-action a ton this season, but Kraft could be the beneficiary whenever they do Sunday.
